4.name: LOOKUP
4.requires: a copy of this image's immutable snapshot-issued state

fields_u64_little_by_offset.112: validated frame count in current pass
fields_u64_little_by_offset.136: committed DB page count, or base page count if no commit
fields_u64_little_by_offset.160: committed byte end offset, or zero
fields_u64_little_by_offset.184: latest matching frame within fixed committed prefix

state.host_contract: Only zeroed state or a prior successful reply state issued by this exact image/session is valid. This is an opaque continuation, not a caller-authorized mutable record.
state.memory_bound: 256 bytes independent of WAL length and database page count

fields_u64_little: request/selected frame number; scan result uses valid frame count

location_tags.0: target exceeds committed/base database page count; no page
location_tags.1: read from base database at the returned byte offset under the same external snapshot
location_tags.2: read page data from the selected WAL frame under the same external snapshot

output.read_authority: Offsets describe requested bytes. They do not perform I/O or acquire permission, locks, descriptor identity or filesystem custody.

scan.extent: Captured file extent is fixed for the pass; bytes appended later are excluded.
scan.short_WAL: extent <=32: no WAL header is read and base DB view remains unchanged, matching walIndexRecover nSize>WAL_HDRSIZE.
scan.invalid_header: Magic/size/checksum failures yield an ignored-WAL snapshot with an explicit reason. Unsupported version refuses; it never silently grants an empty view.
frame_admission: exact transport and internally bound page size
rolling checksum of first8 header bytes then page data
scan.commit: Only a checksum-valid frame whose big-endian dbsize field is nonzero advances committed frame, committed DB size, committed byte offset and committed checksum together.
scan.tail: A short final frame based on captured extent or the first invalid full frame stops the scan. Later valid bytes are never searched to restart a chain. Valid dbsize=0 frames after the last commit are not visible.
scan.checksum_failure_difference: The failed C decoder may modify a transient checksum seed. This core leaves its last valid working seed in state, and exposes only the saved committed seed for snapshot identity. It is not a drop-in mutable Wal object.

lookup.algorithm: Replay exactly the selected committed prefix from the retained header under an externally stable generation; retain only the last matching page position. No unbounded page map is allocated.
lookup.header_binding: All eight 32-bit header fields must match the snapshot. The header checksum is also recomputed.
lookup.end_binding: Final replayed frame index, byte end, nonzero dbsize and rolling checksum must equal the snapshot. Any invalid or changed prefix is a refusal, not an ignored tail.
lookup.after_snapshot: No frame after committed_end_offset is requested or selected.
lookup.out_of_range: Pages above the snapshot DB size return missing without reading WAL.
lookup.no_commit: When committed_frame=0, valid uncommitted frames grant no WAL visibility. Page lookup uses base DB count/size.
lookup.latest_match: Only matching frames at or before the frozen end mark may win. Earlier commits and matching frames within the final committed transaction participate.
lookup.cost: O(number of committed frames) per nontrivial lookup; fixed storage. A future index may optimize this without changing the snapshot rules.

refusals.4294967288: fixed snapshot prefix differs or lookup state cannot match
refusals.4294967289: unsupported WAL version after valid format/checksum
refusals.4294967293: protocol, extent, phase or replay misuse

domains.page_number: 1 through 2^32-1, as the retained byte decoder; pager limits remain external
domains.wal_extent: 0 through 2^63-1, the existing SQLite signed-i64 file-offset representation; no new byte-volume policy limit
domains.frame_number: u64; not restricted to an in-memory wal-index population
domains.fixed_input: one frame <=65560 bytes plus 16-byte command; the SQLite maximum page size is a format limit, not a whole-WAL cap

external_requirements: The scanner input must correspond to one stable database/WAL generation protected by the proper recovery/read locks.
The captured size and each exact read must come from the bound WAL descriptor; read errors must abort and cannot be reported as EOF.
Keep required reader locks through locator replay and the final database/WAL page read; salts and checksums are not cryptographic identity or synchronization.
Admit base DB header geometry, page count, checkpoint/backfill relationship and WAL generation before exposing the page source as a production transaction.
WAL reset, writer serialization, WAL-index shared memory, checkpoints, fsync/durable commit, page mutation and SQL/AgentStore transactions remain external.
hosted_bridge_responsibilities: bounded fresh buffer allocation/copying and object materialization
per-session one-use and permanent closure after errors/caught reentry
native executable source/image/ABI qualification supplied externally
